scope: Proposition 2.8 (One-coordinate projection) of the manuscript “A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem” (preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a102efd4a3009423), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D ≤ X < Y , with Y labelled, and suppose that (X ∩ NY )/FY = PIY X , 1 < PX < TY . Suppose also that X is an intersection of coatoms of [X, Y ]; a coatom itself is allowed. Fix i ∈ IY and let ρ : Yi −→ Aut(TY ) be the action of its factor stabilizer on that coordinate. Identify TY with its inner automorphism group, and put H∗ = ρ(Xi). Then H∗ ∩ TY = PX. (2.6) The saturated overgroups of X form a sublattice of [X, Y ], and Z 7−→ KZ = ρ(Zi) = H∗PZ, (Z ∩ NY )/FY = PIY Z , (2.7) is an isomorphism from that sublattice onto the entire ordinary subgroup interval [H∗, H∗TY ]. Original covering relations between saturated vertices remain covering relations after projection. In particular, a strict change of simple type at a cover yields a maximal subgroup of an almost simple group, supplementing its simple socle.
